scope: Opt-in Core Kimi native device issuer and persisted issuer-bound refresh; native live inference/host binding remains mandatory

reference.meaning: Read the existing pinned source; no new SDK acquisition/execution. Fixed client/device form, mandatory token pair/expiry, Bearer intent and bounded transient refresh policy are source-reviewed, not vendor/account acceptance.

requirements.requirement: Reusable native Kimi device flow rather than a label/config-only issuer
requirements.implementation: Move the existing bounded CLI OAuthDeviceClient into Core, retaining its HTTPS/manual-redirect/UTF-8/response limits, caller cancellation, late-body ownership, pending/slow-down polling and token profiles. CLI keeps its environment adapter/re-exports. Core exports beginKimiCodingDeviceLogin with the frozen public-client config and optional explicit host/fetcher/redactor/signal. Private prompt and issuer are captured before await; public complete verification URI/user code cannot contain registered private code. One-shot completion and cancellation return native credential metadata; SDK owns neither listener/browser nor store publication.
requirements.proof: New Core flow case reserves existing encrypted publication before device work, polls pending→success, commits0600 credentials under a foreign storage label and refuses reuse/ordinary consumer resolution. Native body-stall cancellation does not await hostile cancellation. Existing eight client controls and27 actual emitted CLI authentication/TLS journeys exercise the moved client through its old interfaces. Public compiled SDK smoke imports the root, logs in, refreshes via the credential service and exits normally after three mocked requests.

requirements.requirement: Persisted issuer/realm/grant ownership and guarded refresh
requirements.implementation: ProviderOAuthCredential.subscription admits explicit KimiCodingOAuthIdentity {provider:'kimi-coding',oauthHost,grantId}. Grant UUID is local login identity, not a verified remote account subject; refresh preserves it. Consumers explicitly select subscriptionProvider:'kimi-coding'; ordinary/generic/API-key consumers cannot borrow it. An explicit kimiOAuthHost must match before refresh I/O. Native refresh derives the fixed public client/token URL from stored issuer metadata and ignores generic OAuth endpoint/client-secret hints. Existing revision/CAS/generation/caller publication guards remain authoritative.
requirements.proof: Encrypted expiry/restart refresh preserves local grant and rotating pair against the stored prefixed issuer, not malicious generic hints. Wrong issuer/realm, offline expiry, generic token and environment API-key substitution refuse without refresh. Existing absent-slot logout publication guard and malformed-native-identity cases refuse; expired ciphertext is unchanged by the pre-I/O refusals.

requirements.requirement: Effective bounded native refresh retry and body retirement
requirements.implementation: Only newly marked native Kimi credentials get initial+three maximum attempts with1/2/4s backoff for network errors and429/5xx, within the existing credential-operation timeout.401/403/invalid_grant do not retry. Backoff is caller-cancellable; response handoff/late settlement releases abandoned bodies once without waiting for cancellation. The generic/legacy configured refresh remains single-attempt. Core-owned polling keeps its timer referenced so a standalone SDK await cannot disappear when no other handle is live; delay values/deadlines are unchanged.
requirements.proof: Native retry, exhaustion, three authorization refusals, backoff cancellation and late-refresh-body controls cover the distinct new policy. One bounded old-image retry RED and one late-body RED precede correction. The original emitted SDK exits13 with unsettled top-level await at first poll; removing the inherited CLI-only unref, not adding fixture keepalive or changing a duration, makes the unchanged emitted program pass.
